rv.q: This production is a blaze of colour at a dismally grey time.
I feel like a heel for saying it but this Kinky Boots is soulless.

Kinky Boots approaches gender and sexuality in a warm, good-humoured way, and lightly explores themes of fathers and sons, expectations and acceptance. Harvey Fierstein’s book offers a fair amount of “tell don’t show” along the way. “We may have been born in a small factory town but I sure as hell don’t intend to stay!” Charlie’s fiance explains.
Radebe and Cardle knock this Kinky Boots out of the park.
Everyone gives their absolute all to ensure the audience have a jolly good time.

Often described as a “fierce” and “fabulous” show, this revival of Kinky Boots has certainly strutted its way to London with Matt Cardle and Johannes Radebe featuring prominently on posters heralding its arrival.
Joyous and uplifting, Kinky Boots is just the tonic in an increasingly divided and divisive world.
But neither book nor songs offer enough to buy a ticket to a show that leans lazily into the North in Northampton - complete with flat caps, vests and tats, and wayward accents.

cn.t: Johannes Radebe dazzles in this energetic revival, elevating a formulaic musical with his magnetic star power. Critics find the show itself mediocre and paint-by-numbers, but praise Foster's production for breathing new life into it.

dr.inst: Rush tickets released daily at 10 AM via TodayTix app only. Until 11 July 2026.
